title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
agent_writes: Hierarchical Python policies that compose perception, planning, and control APIs.
feedback: Runtime perception consumed by the generated program
No post-rollout code-repair loop in the original system
final_artifact: An executable Python policy program.
evaluation: Tabletop manipulation, whiteboard drawing, and mobile manipulation across physical robot platforms.
summary: The foundational CaP formulation: repurpose a language model's code prior to synthesize inspectable robot policies over a curated API.

title: How to Prompt Your Robot: A PromptBook for Manipulation Skills with Code as Policies
agent_writes: Robot policy code and new low-level manipulation skills under alternative prompt designs.
feedback: State-estimation outputs supplied in the prompt
final_artifact: Executable manipulation-skill code.
evaluation: Prompt-component ablations and new-skill execution on a mobile manipulator.
summary: A systematic study of how examples, instructions, chain-of-thought, and state estimation shape CaP skill generation.

title: RoboScript: Code Generation for Free-Form Manipulation Tasks across Real and Simulation
agent_writes: Deployable manipulation code against a unified ROS and Gazebo interface.
final_artifact: Robot-executable manipulation code.
evaluation: A free-form manipulation benchmark plus end-to-end evaluations on Franka and UR5 embodiments in simulation and reality.
summary: Moves CaP from idealized APIs toward deployability by unifying code generation, perception, planning, control, and simulation checks.

title: RoboCodeX: Multimodal Code Generation for Robotic Behavior Synthesis
agent_writes: Tree-structured robot code built from object-centric manipulation units with affordance and safety constraints.
final_artifact: Executable object-centric robot behavior code.
evaluation: Four manipulation categories and one navigation task in simulators and on real robots.
summary: Uses multimodal, tree-structured code generation to translate scene understanding into deployable behavior across tasks and embodiments.

title: GenCHiP: Generating Robot Policy Code for High-Precision and Contact-Rich Manipulation Tasks
agent_writes: Policy code over compliant motion primitives with force, stiffness, and pose constraints.
final_artifact: Executable policy code for precision and contact-rich manipulation.
evaluation: Subtasks derived from the Functional Manipulation Benchmark and NIST task boards under perception and grasp noise.
summary: Shows that the action-space abstraction can determine whether generated policy code handles precise, contact-rich tasks.

title: RoboCoder: Robotic Learning from Basic Skills to General Tasks with Large Language Models
agent_writes: Action code that composes basic skills for progressively harder simulated tasks.
final_artifact: Refined executable action code.
evaluation: Eighty manually designed tasks across seven simulated entities, including a humanoid setting.
summary: An early closed-loop coding framework that updates action programs from environment feedback instead of relying only on one-shot synthesis.

title: Robotic Programmer: Video Instructed Policy Code Generation for Robotic Manipulation
agent_writes: Executable robot policy code that invokes an embodiment-specific skill API.
final_artifact: A policy program for zero-shot manipulation.
evaluation: Zero-shot manipulation on RLBench and LIBERO plus real-world experiments and API-variation tests.
summary: Trains a multimodal code generator on 115,000 Video2Code examples, making code synthesis itself the learned robot capability.

title: Embodied Long Horizon Manipulation with Closed-loop Code Generation and Incremental Few-shot Adaptation
agent_writes: Executable long-horizon code plans rather than natural-language subtask lists.
final_artifact: A replanned executable manipulation program.
evaluation: More than 30 seen and unseen tasks across LoHoRavens, CALVIN, Franka Kitchen, and cluttered real settings.
summary: DAHLIA closes the loop around executable code plans with a multimodal reporter and incremental few-shot memory.

title: GenSwarm: Scalable Multi-Robot Code-Policy Generation and Deployment via Language Models
agent_writes: Python skill libraries, skill graphs, and deployable code policies for multi-robot systems.
final_artifact: A verified multi-robot code policy and reusable skill graph.
evaluation: Simulated and physical multi-robot tasks, including altered and unseen instructions, against agent and CaP baselines.
summary: Extends CaP to multi-robot deployment with specialized language agents, a skill graph, simulation validation, and hardware translation.

title: HyCodePolicy: Hybrid Language Controllers for Multimodal Monitoring and Decision in Embodied Agents
agent_writes: Checkpointed manipulation programs that can be revised after execution failures.
final_artifact: A repaired executable manipulation program.
evaluation: RoboTwin 1.0 and Bi2Code comparisons against one-shot CaP and CodeAct-style baselines.
summary: Pairs code execution with multimodal checkpoint monitoring so a language controller can diagnose and repair failed plans.

title: Growing with Your Embodied Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Lifelong Code Generation Framework for Long-Horizon Manipulation Skills
agent_writes: Long-horizon manipulation code and reusable skills distilled from human corrections.
feedback: Retrieval from an external skill memory
final_artifact: Executable task code plus a persistent reusable skill library.
evaluation: Ravens, Franka Kitchen, MetaWorld, and real-world long-horizon tasks, including programs spanning more than 20 primitives.
summary: Turns localized human corrections into retrievable program skills, making lifelong CaP memory explicit and editable.

title: Towards Reliable Code-as-Policies: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Embodied Task Planning
agent_writes: Task code plus exploratory programs that acquire missing observations.
final_artifact: A symbolically checked, environment-grounded task program.
evaluation: Dynamic and partially observable RLBench tasks plus real-world experiments.
summary: Adds explicit verification and active information gathering to reduce grounding failures in generated robot programs.

title: ALRM: Agentic LLM for Robotic Manipulation
agent_writes: Executable Code-as-Policy controllers or ReAct-style tool calls under a shared benchmark.
feedback: ReAct reasoning traces in the tool-policy setting
final_artifact: An executable control program or online tool-use policy.
evaluation: Fifty-six manipulation tasks across multiple simulated environments, model families, and language variants.
summary: A broad benchmark that compares code generation and online tool use as two agentic control interfaces.

title: Act-Observe-Rewrite: Multimodal Coding Agents as In-Context Policy Learners for Robot Manipulation
agent_writes: An entire low-level Python controller class rewritten between robot episodes.
final_artifact: A revised low-level controller implementation.
evaluation: Three robosuite UR5e manipulation tasks with sandboxing, action clamps, and rollback.
summary: Makes the full controller, rather than a skill sequence, the unit of multimodal diagnosis and test-time rewrite.

title: CaP-X: A Framework for Benchmarking and Improving Coding Agents for Robot Manipulation
agent_writes: Robot programs and automatically synthesized skills over perception and control primitives.
final_artifact: An iteratively repaired policy program and optional skill library.
evaluation: CaP-Gym with 187 tasks; CaP-Bench across 12 models; simulation, real embodiments, and sim-to-real experiments.
summary: Turns CaP into a controlled agent benchmark and shows how abstraction quality and test-time computation jointly determine reliability.

title: RHO: Your Coding Agent is Secretly a Roboticist
agent_writes: Interpretable multi-file repositories containing prompts, tools, wrappers, routing, and control code.
final_artifact: A pre-deployment-optimized neurosymbolic policy repository.
evaluation: LIBERO-Pro, robosuite, and held-out O3DE tasks, including single-turn deployment and harness-efficiency measures.
summary: Expands the policy artifact from one program to a repository, shifting expensive search before deployment while retaining fixed execution.

title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
agent_writes: Self-proposed task programs and persistent skills distilled from verified retries during play.
final_artifact: A frozen reusable code-skill library plus task programs.
evaluation: LIBERO-Pro, MolmoSpaces, cross-environment robosuite transfer, and zero-shot physical-robot transfer.
summary: RATs uses autonomous play to discover, repair, verify, and distill program skills that transfer beyond the training environment.

title: ASPIRE: Agentic Skills Discovery for Robotics
agent_writes: Robot programs, validated repairs, and parameterized skills that persist across tasks.
final_artifact: A continually expanding library of verified program skills.
evaluation: LIBERO-Pro, robosuite, BEHAVIOR-1K, unseen long-horizon tasks, and cross-embodiment real-robot transfer.
summary: Treats external code memory as continual learning: verified repairs are abstracted into reusable skills rather than folded into model weights.

title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness for Variational Automation Tasks
agent_writes: Directed computation graphs whose nodes are modular perception, planning, and control skills.
final_artifact: A rehearsed computation graph deployed as the robot policy.
evaluation: Eight new variational-automation benchmarks: four simulated and four physical.
summary: Replaces a monolithic policy script with an editable computation graph and uses generated simulations to rehearse candidate structures.

title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents
agent_writes: Task programs, primitive bindings, retry logic, and memories around a frozen VLA.
final_artifact: An agent harness that composes analytic primitives with a retryable VLA primitive.
evaluation: Perturbed LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa365, and RoboTwin C2R simulation benchmarks.
summary: A clean division of labor: the coding agent handles semantics, long-horizon recovery, and memory while the frozen VLA handles local contact-rich motion.

title: MEMENTO: Memory-Guided Memetic Code-as-Policy Evolution
agent_writes: Executable policies and rollout evaluators evolved through mutation, crossover, and memory.
final_artifact: An evolved executable policy and its learned evaluator.
evaluation: Robosuite Tower of Hanoi, AI2-THOR tasks, held-out variants, and sim-to-real transfer to a Franka robot.
summary: Uses memetic search to evolve both policy code and the evaluator that directs subsequent code mutations.

title: A Few Words Go a Long Way: Language Guided Robot Policy Synthesis
agent_writes: Modular robot programs and persistent skills grounded from localized language corrections.
final_artifact: An executable policy program plus a reusable skill library.
evaluation: Physical Franka tasks spanning long horizons, articulated-object manipulation, and cloth folding.
summary: ARCHITECT frames robot policy acquisition as interactive program synthesis, localizing human feedback to editable code and reusable skills.

title: Claude Plays Robotics
strictness_note: A capability and interface study rather than a standalone CaP method; included because one evaluated interface asks the model to write robot controllers.
agent_writes: Python controllers in the programmatic-control condition; other conditions use direct, learned-policy, or high-level interfaces.
final_artifact: Controller code in one evaluation condition.
evaluation: A cross-interface capability study spanning classical control, legged robots, and manipulation in simulation, with separate physical-robot demonstrations.
summary: Useful evidence that embodiment, abstraction, and control frequency can dominate apparent model capability; it is not a new CaP algorithm.

title: Introducing Waddle: Agents that Control Robots
strictness_note: A product research post with real-hardware demonstrations and internal evaluations, but without a paper-level benchmark protocol or reproducible release.
agent_writes: Task programs and parameterized skills that compose fixed perception and control primitives or call action models.
final_artifact: A runnable task program plus skills shared across deployed agents.
evaluation: Real-hardware demonstrations, an internal model comparison, and a reported overnight run of roughly 1,000 LEGO operations used to train ACT.
summary: A productized CaP stack that combines long-horizon coding agents, shared skills, VLA calls, data collection, and real-robot iteration.

title: Telekinesis Physical AI Agents
strictness_note: The documentation describes executable, reviewable CaP over a large skill library, but does not provide a controlled robot-learning evaluation.
agent_writes: Readable Python programs that compose existing robot skills and generate new skills when needed.
final_artifact: A reviewable Python robot program.
evaluation: Product examples and application demos; no controlled empirical benchmark is documented.
summary: An industrially oriented CaP product centered on typed, auditable skills and human review before hardware execution.
